title: The brief and review loop needs no PR comment: local round records, bounded context packs and situation coverage
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-28 worker rounds took 20-70 minutes and 150-290 model turns, mostly re-reading 2,000-3,800-line files to find what failed. Rounds whose brief named the failing lines and the root cause finished in about 20 minutes. The captain: firstmate coordinates and must hand the worker enough to fix the problem, not make it hunt. firstmate writes such briefs by hand today; this task makes fm-worker.sh assemble the evidence itself for every round, so no round starts blind. The captain approved the direction on 2026-09-28, and the coverage check by situation, warning first, the same day. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-135.json, is committed on this branch.

The context pack. Before a round on an existing pull request, fm-worker.sh (outside the sandbox, with the operator's gh) builds a file the prompt includes: (1) for a red or cancelled required check, each failing assertion's name, its log lines (via the job log, by byte range when large) and, located by the assertion's message, the test source around it (file:line and about 20 lines); a cancelled run says which stage was running and for how long; (2) the latest review's findings, each with the file:line it cites and those lines from the head; (3) the spec acceptance items each finding or failure touches; (4) the PR's merge state (BEHIND, DIRTY) and, when DIRTY, the conflicting paths. Bounded in size (a stated cap, largest items trimmed first, never silently dropped: a trimmed item says so).

firstmate's approved local brief still leads. T-135 owns append-only round records under state/evidence/<project>/<task>/, written by trusted fm outside rounds. Each record carries project, task, round, actor, kind (brief, pack, worker-report, ask, verdict), head SHA, time and text; verdicts carry T-163 authenticated final-answer provenance and reviewer identity. Read the latest authorized brief for the exact project/task/round and head; the pack follows it, never replaces it. The worker starts with both before reading files. A PR comment is an optional projection, never a source or prerequisite. Existing state/briefs/ files alone are not script-consumed evidence; firstmate must supply an approved record through this writer. T-135 has no external prerequisite; T-138 later extends this same layout to FM_HOME and adds spec/patch binding, without a record-layout migration.

Brief coverage, by situation, as a warning first. Before a round, fm-worker.sh classifies it and checks coverage rather than format: (a) a first round with no pull request: the spec itself is the brief, so it checks the spec: a Why is present, every file its acceptance names or implies a change to is inside its scope (T-121 lost a round to this), every path it names exists, its dependencies are merged; (b) after a red required check: every failing assertion is mentioned in firstmate's approved local brief or in the context pack; (c) after a cancelled check: the brief or pack says which stage ran and for how long; (d) after a REJECT: every numbered finding is answered, as fix or as deferred with a reason; (e) a branch that only needs updating with its base needs no brief; (f) a scope or requirement change by the captain: the brief quotes the captain's words and the task file's scope matches. An item firstmate cannot or should not cover is marked in the brief as `deferred: <reason>`, and a whole round as `no brief needed: <reason>`; either is recorded as an event and shown on the board. A gap is a warning on the board (en and zh-TW) naming the uncovered item; it does not block the round. Whether any situation later blocks is the captain's call, from the recorded rounds: the event log keeps, per round, the situation, the gaps, the turns and the duration, so the effect of complete briefs can be shown. Tests cover each situation, a deferred item, a waived round, and that a gap warns without blocking.

Tests (fail first, stubs answering as gh does): a red run's failing assertion and its source lines reach the prompt; a cancelled run is reported as such; review findings arrive with their cited lines; a DIRTY PR lists its conflicting paths; the size cap trims visibly. Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Workers do not run the suites themselves.

T-135 owns the local readers: fm-worker.sh builds the next prompt from the local brief, pack, authenticated verdict and standing list; it retains .fm-say.md reports/questions and ASK-PASS-CRITERIA as local records before optional publication. fm-review.sh supplies the standing list and relevant prior rounds from local records to every reviewer from round two, excluding worker reasoning. Every REJECT from round one supplies the complete numbered list and CRITERIA-COMPLETE; an ask is only for a missing or unclear list, before edits, with no delayed round threshold. Gate 7 and fm-protocol.sh read the latest authenticated local verdict/list, preserve latest-REJECT precedence, numbering and done/open states, and allow new items only as REGRESSION or NEW-GROUND. Missing local verdict fails gate 7 with its reason; quoted markers and stale PR comments are never fallback authority. Syntax checks do not prove finding semantics. T-073's PR-comment transport is historical.

Evidence: required GitHub checks and commit statuses plus six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7 on the authoritative current PR head; gate 3 is retired. Workers author feature-owned fail-first tests but run no suites. Tests stay at most 1200 lines; shared fixtures in tests/lib/ or tests/e2e/lib/, with literal helper references. Firstmate verifies CI/gates and real acceptance; a structure check cannot prove model compliance. Commit this task spec with implementation.

Pending or missing checks within the wait bound differ from failed/cancelled checks; carry check-runs and commit statuses with exact head/source. Packs stay in local project state. Authenticate final verdict/identity before treating quoted lists as criteria. Missing evidence warns visibly, never fabricates coverage. Independent evidence/brief work may run in parallel with coordinated shared-file ownership.

A project-level projection setting in config.yaml, resolved by fm-config.sh, selects comments or local independently of external conventions; the self project defaults to comments for compatibility. Both modes retain the same authoritative local records. With local, no round record is posted and the entire brief -> worker -> review -> gate 7 loop works. With comments, publication is an optional projection after durable recording; report publication failures and preserve records. T-140 later adds summary, check and threads; T-138 extends external storage. Test a full local loop with a gh stub refusing every comment write, a stale contradictory PR comment, missing/stale/unauthorized local briefs, and a missing local verdict failing gate 7 with its reason. Cover round-one REJECT criteria and round-two prompt delivery, authentic final-answer selection, later rejection precedence and closed-list violations. Preserve first-round spec-as-brief and warn honestly about missing evidence. Deferred/waived records and gap warnings carry authored en and zh-TW summaries; dictionaries only label static controls.

Captain revision 2026-10-02: brief and review must not require permission to post each round work log to the external repository. T-135 runs in the first wave beside T-142 with depends_on: []; no CONVENTIONS.md or T-138 contract is required for its comments/local loop. Keep project/task identities distinct, local artifacts private, and coordinate shared worker/reviewer/library files with immutable run snapshots.
